bam.help:
usage: wgsextract bam [-h] <command> ...

positional arguments:
  <command>
    sort      Sort alignments by genomic coordinates. Required by almost all downstream tools
              (like variant callers) to function correctly.
    index     Create a random-access index (.bai/.crai) for your file. This allows tools to jump
              to specific regions instantly without reading the whole file.
    unindex   Remove the index file associated with your BAM/CRAM. Use this to force a re-indexing
              or to clean up workspace.
    unsort    Mark the file as 'unsorted' in the header. Rarely needed, but useful if a tool
              requires a specific header state for processing.
    to-cram   Convert BAM to the modern CRAM format. Highly recommended for long-term storage as
              it is ~30-50% smaller than BAM without losing data.
    to-bam    Convert a CRAM file back to the traditional BAM format. Useful if you need to use an
              older tool that doesn't support CRAM.
    unalign   Extract raw reads from a BAM/CRAM back into FASTQ format. Use this if you want to
              re-align your data to a different reference genome.
    identify  Analyze your BAM header to determine exactly which reference genome was used for the
              original alignment.
    merge     Merge several coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files (e.g. per-lane files) aligned to the
              same reference into one indexed file.
    to-ubam   Convert an aligned BAM/CRAM or FASTQ reads into a queryname-sorted unaligned BAM
              (uBAM) for GATK pipelines.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

actions.help: show this help message and exit

help: sort
Sort alignments by genomic coordinates. Required by almost all downstream tools (like variant callers) to function correctly.
index
Create a random-access index (.bai/.crai) for your file. This allows tools to jump to specific regions instantly without reading the whole file.
unindex
Remove the index file associated with your BAM/CRAM. Use this to force a re-indexing or to clean up workspace.
unsort
Mark the file as 'unsorted' in the header. Rarely needed, but useful if a tool requires a specific header state for processing.
to-cram
Convert BAM to the modern CRAM format. Highly recommended for long-term storage as it is ~30-50%% smaller than BAM without losing data.
to-bam
Convert a CRAM file back to the traditional BAM format. Useful if you need to use an older tool that doesn't support CRAM.
unalign
Extract raw reads from a BAM/CRAM back into FASTQ format. Use this if you want to re-align your data to a different reference genome.
identify
Analyze your BAM header to determine exactly which reference genome was used for the original alignment.
merge
Merge several coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files (e.g. per-lane files) aligned to the same reference into one indexed file.
to-ubam
Convert an aligned BAM/CRAM or FASTQ reads into a queryname-sorted unaligned BAM (uBAM) for GATK pipelines.

bam merge.help:
usage: wgsextract bam merge [-h] [--output OUTPUT] [--cram] [--attach-rg] FILE [FILE ...]

positional arguments:
  FILE             Coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files aligned to the same reference.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --output OUTPUT  Output file name or path (a bare name goes in --outdir; default: merged.bam, or
                   merged.cram with --cram).
  --cram           Write CRAM instead of BAM.
  --attach-rg      Tag each read with a read group named after its input file, for inputs without
                   @RG lines (so reads stay traceable to their lane).

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

examples:
  wgsextract bam merge lane1.bam lane2.bam --output sample.bam

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  merged.bam or merged.cram (+ index), or the --output path.

needs:
  samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; hours on a 30x
  genome.

extract.help:
usage: wgsextract extract [-h] <command> ...

positional arguments:
  <command>
    mito-fasta    Extract the Mitochondrial DNA (chrM) consensus sequence. Compatible with yFull
                  (female-only mtDNA upload) and other sequence analysis tools. (Format: .FASTA)
    mito-vcf      Call variants specifically for the mitochondrial DNA. Used by Mitoverse
                  (Haplogrep) for haplogroup classification. (Format: .VCF)
    mt-bam        Isolate all mitochondrial-related reads into a new, smaller BAM file. Used for
                  high-resolution mtDNA analysis or maternal haplogroup prediction on services
                  like Mitoverse (Haplogrep). (Format: .BAM)
    ydna-bam      Extract all Y-chromosome reads into a separate BAM file. Compatible with yDNA
                  Warehouse, yTree, and specialized paternal lineage tools. (Format: .BAM)
    ydna-vcf      Call variants specifically for the Y-chromosome. Used by services like
                  Cladefinder for haplogroup prediction. (Format: .VCF)
    y-mt-extract  Extract both Y-chromosome and Mitochondrial reads into a single, combined BAM
                  file. Recommended for yFull (male-only) WGS uploads. (Format: .BAM)
    unmapped      Extract reads that did not align to the reference. Often used to find viral
                  contamination or non-human DNA using services like Kaiju and CosmosID.
    custom        Extract reads from a specific chromosomal region or gene of interest.
    bam-subset    (advanced) Create a smaller version of your BAM file using a random fraction of
                  reads (e.g. 0.1 for 10%). Useful for testing pipelines quickly.

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

actions.help: show this help message and exit

report.help:
usage: wgsextract report [-h] [--workspace DIR] [--results DIR] [--format {tsv,parquet}]

Summarise a sample's results (overview, QC, lineage, pharmacogenomics, ClinVar pathogenic calls in
ACMG SF genes, microarray files) as a local HTML, Markdown and JSON report with confidence-
labelled findings. Reads earlier runs' result manifests; runs no analysis and makes no network
calls. Technical results, not diagnosis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --workspace DIR       Sample folder whose results are reported (default: the --genome folder,
                        else the --input's folder).
  --results DIR         Also read result manifests from this folder (repeatable); only runs on
                        this sample's files are used. The --outdir is always read.
  --format {tsv,parquet}
                        Format of the findings table, <sample>_personal_report_findings.tsv or
                        .parquet (needs pyarrow) (default: tsv)

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

examples:
  wgsextract report --genome HG002
  wgsextract report --input sample.cram
  wgsextract report --workspace HG002 --results ~/wgs-out/HG002 --format parquet

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  <sample>_personal_report.html, .md and .json and
  <sample>_personal_report_findings.tsv (or .parquet with --format parquet) in
  the sample folder (or --outdir); evidence links are relative to the sample
  folder.

needs:
  no external tools; seconds from existing results.

vcf indel.help:
usage: wgsextract vcf indel [-h] [-r REGION] [--parallel] [--help-all]

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  -r, --region REGION  Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000)
  --parallel           Call contigs in parallel with up to --threads workers. SNP calling then
                       recalls the stretches with sites deeper than 255 reads in one stream,
                       because bcftools subsamples them with one random stream per process, so the
                       calls match the default single stream.
  --help-all           Show this help with the advanced options too, and exit.

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

3 advanced options not shown; 'wgsextract vcf indel --help-all' lists them.

examples:
  wgsextract vcf indel --input sample.cram

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  indels.vcf.gz (+ .tbi).

needs:
  bcftools, samtools, tabix; hours on a 30x genome.

actions.help: show this help message and exit
File defining ploidy per chromosome (auto-resolved from --ref if possible)

Call contigs in parallel with up to --threads workers. SNP calling then recalls the stretches with sites deeper than 255 reads in one stream, because bcftools subsamples them with one random stream per process, so the calls match the default single stream.
Warn below this mean depth for this run; 0 disables (default: config qc_min_diploid_depth 15, or qc_min_haploid_depth 3 for chrY/mtDNA)
Show this help with the advanced options too, and exit.
